overview: Often considered the first independent Thai kingdom, Sukhothai is known for its benevolent paternal kingship and the creation of the Thai alphabet. It produced elegant walking Buddha sculptures and distinctive lotus-bud stupas that defined Thai artistic identity.

items.text: King Ram Khamhaeng creates the Thai alphabet, adapting Khmer and Mon scripts.
The walking Buddha sculpture, a uniquely Thai innovation, conveys grace and spiritual movement.
Lotus-bud stupas and Sri Lankan-style chedis define the Sukhothai architectural style.
Theravada Buddhism from Sri Lanka adopted as the state religion.
Ram Khamhaeng's inscription describes a paternal king who hears subjects' grievances by bell.
Sukhothai Historical Park is a UNESCO World Heritage site.
The Thai alphabet remains in use today with minor modifications.

fall.text: Sukhothai was absorbed as a vassal state by the rising Ayutthaya Kingdom.
